Lieutenant Greywand was an elite gnome serving the Alliance in Alterac Valley. He guarded the Stonehearth Outpost along with Lieutenant Largent.

Lieutenant Commander's Battlegear was an Alliance six-piece PvP-Rare Warrior set. Various pieces were available for purchase at Ranks 7, 8 and 10 from Captain Dirgehammer, located in the Champions' Hall of Stormwind. This set is no longer available and was replaced by Lieutenant Commander's Battlearmor, however, items from either set contribute toward the bonuses of both sets.

Lieutenant Commander's Aegis was an Alliance six-piece PvP-Rare Paladin set. Various pieces were available for purchase at Ranks 7, 8 and 10 from Captain Dirgehammer, located in the Champions' Hall of Stormwind. This set is no longer available and was replaced by Lieutenant Commander's Redoubt, however, items from either set contribute toward the bonuses of both sets.

Various pieces were available for purchase at Ranks 7, 8 and 10 from Captain Dirgehammer, located in the Champions' Hall of Stormwind. This set is no longer available and was replaced by Lieutenant Commander's Refuge, however items from either set contribute toward the bonuses of both sets.

Lieutenant Commander's Chain Pauldrons is mail shoulder armor for hunters. Lifebloom is a Restoration druid heal over time (HoT) spell. If Lifebloom completes its duration or is dispelled, it will bloom and immediately heal the target. Lifebloom can only be cast on one target at a time. If cast on another target the previous Lifebloom will vanish without blooming.

Lieutenant Alverold was one of Daelin Proudmoore's lieutenants and made up a part of the fleet which sailed to Durotar in search of Jaina Proudmoore. While Proudmoore headed towards land, he ordered Alverold to take an exploratory fleet and scout out the coasts of Kalimdor. Meanwhile, Daelin did battle with the Horde, and was killed by Rexxar and his comrades. Lieutenant Benedict continued Daelin's campaign, and Admiral Proudmoore's Orders dictated that Alverold had to reinforce him eventually. Alverold's fate is unknown.
Lieutenant Maeve is a dwarf quest giver located at Fort Wildervar in the Howling Fjord.

Light's Trust is an Argent Crusade base camp located in the northeast corner of Dragonblight, just outside Jintha'kalar. It was established in an ancient Drakkari temple captured by the crusaders.

Light's Point is the beach to the east of Light's Point Tower and Havenshire in the Scarlet Enclave. During Massacre At Light's Point, new death knight characters slaughter hundreds of Scarlet Crusade members here.

Light's Breach is a small encampment belonging to the Argent Crusade and is located north of Drak'Tharon Keep in Zul'Drak. As the smaller of the Argent Crusade’s bases in Zul’Drak, it occupies an abandoned courtyard surrounded by broken walls and was founded at the time of the war against the Lich King. Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that the encampment is still active as a position to repel the Scourge in the region.

Life of a Peasant, abbreviated as 'LOAP', was an early roleplaying custom map in Warcraft III. While it was never a roaring success as Defense of the Ancients was and still is, LOAP has become one of the most edited custom maps on Warcraft III.

Light's Heart is the sentience core of the naaru prime Xe'ra sent as a last resort by High Exarch Turalyon who battles on Argus, to be handed to Prophet Velen. It fell from the Felstorm along the coast of Suramar, in the Broken Isles. The Order of the Silver Hand witnessed the event and informed Archmage Khadgar, who then tasked order leaders with recovering it before the Burning Legion did. It has since been kept safe in a class order hall. Unlocked by the Tear of Elune, Xe'ra communicates through it with the order leader in order to provide insight into the history of Illidan Stormrage. She revealed that Light's Heart was to serve as the vessel for Illidan Stormrage's rebirth. After Illida

The Light's Chosen (or simply the Chosen) are an elite order of draenei paladins commanded by Prophet Velen, the leader of the draenei race. First seen some time after the arrival of the draenei on Azeroth, the Light's Chosen have since played a role in resisting the third invasion of the Burning Legion. When the demons attacked the draenei capital of the Exodar, the Light's Chosen fought by Velen's side during the ensuing battle, ultimately prevailing. The exact nature of the order and the extent of its membership is unclear, however they likely serve as personal agents to the Prophet in his quest to preserve the Light.

Life quests were a type of epic race-specific questlines which were planned to be included in the original World of Warcraft. Each life quest told the story of its respective race and what their purpose in the world is, often continuing the story set up in the "smaller" regular quests. For example, the undead life quest revolved around their effort to develop a new plague and would have involved rescuing the undead player character's father from captivity, while the orc life quest would give players a taste of the demonic influence from their past and force them to combat it. The Lightning's Blade clan was an orc clan that dwelled in northeastern Gorgrond. It had strong ties to the Thunderlord clan. After the Horde had conquered much of Draenor, the threat of starvation caused many orcs to turn on each other, clashing in short-lived battles that left hundreds dead. The Lightning's Blade was one of the clans who suffered greatly in these conflicts. When the Horde invaded Azeroth, the Lightning's Blade were left behind on Draenor. After the war, Ner'zhul attempted to reforge the Horde with a promise of new worlds, and managed to attain the partial loyalty of the Lightning's Blade.

A Light Armor Kit is applied to armor to increase the item's armor value by a value of +1. It can only be attached to chest armor, boots, leg armor, or gloves. Armor kits fill the same virtual "slot" as enchantments and will overwrite any existing enchantments, or be overwritten by enchantments applied later.

Lightning Hammers are enchanted hammers crafted by orc shamans in tribute to the warchief, Thrall. Tribal warriors who perform deeds of exceptional skill and bravery sometimes receive a lightning hammer as a reward. Each lightning hammer is a throwing hammer no longer than an orc's forearm. A fist-sized copper hammer head tops a black wooden haft wrapped with copper wire. Shamans sometimes string colored beads or small tokens on the wire, to represent the tribe’s colors or the great deeds of the warrior who now carries the weapon.
Light Parchment can be purchased from an inscription supplier or some trade suppliers.

Lighthouses can be found near ports and coastlines. They are used to warn ships of cliffs and rocks, and are very valuable to whoever controls them. Most of the Lighthouses found in Azeroth are under the control of the Alliance. There are several lighthouse models. The Gilneans had their own type. Stormwind had a newer, larger model, and Auberdine has a night elf design.

The Lightning Sons seem to be a group of far seers in Nagrand, Outland. They are part of the Mag'har. They send Horde players to Sunspring Post, the only other settlement of Mag'har in the area besides Garadar, to fight the enemy — the Murkblood tribe of Broken — who have taken it over. In one of their quests, you meet the enigmatic Saurfang the Younger who Farseer Corhuk refers to as a "youngling".
Lightning Struck is a dungeon & raids achievement earned for defeating General Bjarngrim in the Halls of Lightning on Heroic difficulty while he has a Temporary Electrical Charge.

The Lightless Reaches is an underwater trench and acts as a border between the Shimmering Expanse and Kelp'thar Forest. The water currents through here are said to be very strong. Seahorses can be found swimming through here. As it wraps around within the Shimmering Expanse it serves to separate Biel'aran Ridge from the main portion of the underwater zone.

Lightning Ledge is a section of Wolf's Run taken over by the Twilight's Hammer in Mount Hyjal. It can be found directly above Gar'gol's Hovel south of the Shrine of Goldrinn. The road has been converted into a large makeshift camp with a flamegate built to another realm.
